prompt: A surveyor knows two angles of a triangular plot and the length of the side BETWEEN those two angles, and the same three parts of a second plot match exactly. Which criterion proves the plots are congruent?
hint: Record the known parts in the order you meet them walking around the triangle.

hints.text: Record the known parts in the order you meet them walking around the triangle.
Angle, then the side between them, then angle: A-S-A.

explanation: The known side lies between the two known angles, so reading around the triangle gives Angle-Side-Angle.
That is ASA, a valid congruence criterion.
AAS would apply if the known side were NOT between the two angles, and AAA is not a congruence criterion at all — it only gives similarity.

alternativeExplanations.title: ASA vs AAS in one question
steps: Ask only this: is the known side sandwiched between the two known angles?
Yes → ASA. No → AAS. Here the surveyor measured the side between the angles, so it is ASA.
